newsitem.title: UK: EUROPE SOUR CRUDES SAG AS IRAQ FLOWS, BONN SELLS.
newsitem.headline: EUROPE SOUR CRUDES SAG AS IRAQ FLOWS, BONN SELLS.

text.p: Sour Russian Urals crude was beginning to sag on European markets on Wednesday with the first Iraqi exports since late May only hours away, traders said.
Germany's first sales from its strategic stockpile were adding to bearish sentiment.
The VLCC Arcadia was preparing to berth at the Turkish port of Ceyhan to take on 2.1 million barrels of Iraqi Kirkuk crude for U.S. trader Bayoil.
Loading was expected to begin around midnight (2000 GMT), a port official told Reuters.

While most of the early Kirkuk loadings, the first oil to be sold by Baghdad under the second phase of the U.N.'s oil-for-food deal, were committed, cargoes loading later in the month were being offered to European buyers.
The first five vessels due to load a total of six million barrels of Kirkuk by August 18 are either sold or destined for their lifters' systems, three to the U.S. and one each to France and Spain.
But barrels earmarked for a U.S. major and Russian oil companies were being shown.
"There are a couple of million barrels of Kirkuk being offered at premiums to the contract price," said a trader.
The U.N. approved price formula for August Kirkuk is Dated Brent -$1.90 a barrel fob Ceyhan for European markets, an attractive proposition despite weakening Urals values.
"They could ask for 20 cents more than that and it would still be competitive," said a trader.

Large Urals cargoes loading towards the end of the month were pegged around Dated Brent -$1.00/-95 cents a barrel cif Augusta on Wednesday but smaller and prompter parcels were worth about 20 cents more, traders said.
"There is a lot of talk of two-tier pricing at the moment, before and after Kirkuk barrels come out, but what is clear is that by the third decade Urals will have been forced lower," said a trader.

The benchmark sour crude was in relatively short supply in the near term with only one 80,000-tonne cargo loading around August 20 seen on offer after a similar sized vessel was taken into a major's system.

But with the floodgates opening -- Iraq is planning to export close to 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) until the end of this month -- traders said bigger Urals stems loading late in the month would do well to fetch Dated Brent -$1.20.
The grade was faring little better in northern Europe where sour crudes were also under pressure, traders said.
Urals was pegged at around Dated Brent -90 cents cif NWE amid slack demand and was also starting to feel the impact of Germany's strategic stock sales.
"Sour crudes in the north are certainly struggling. It's beginning to look a bit crowded out there," said a trader.
The first tranche of German reserves -- some 2.8 million barrels of a mixture of sour Iranian Heavy, Saudi Light and Iraqi Kirkuk -- was sold to four companies in a tender on Tuesday.
All the oil is expected to be taken into refining systems in Germany, Sweden and the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp region.
--Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
